agent-context-engineering.name: Agent context engineering
agent-context-engineering.what: Deciding what an agent's context window actually holds — including whether to mount knowledge as a filesystem it reads on demand versus pre-rendering it into the system prompt, trading tokens against tool calls.

agent-hooks.name: Agent hooks
agent-hooks.what: Deterministic scripts that fire at fixed points in a coding agent's tool-call lifecycle to allow, block or steer actions.

agent-quality-monitoring.name: Agent quality monitoring
agent-quality-monitoring.what: Continuously sampling and reviewing a production agent's sessions, clustering failures and tracking whether fixes stick.

ai-vulnerability-discovery.name: AI vulnerability discovery
ai-vulnerability-discovery.what: Using frontier models to scan code for exploitable bugs, with proofs of concept and suggested patches, in the style of OSS-Fuzz.

asr-vocabulary-biasing.name: ASR vocabulary biasing
asr-vocabulary-biasing.what: Supplying domain terms and proper nouns to a speech-to-text pipeline so it stops substituting phonetically similar, more common words.

assignment-problems.name: Assignment problems
assignment-problems.what: The optimisation class behind 'which shard on which host' — matching items to slots at minimum cost, solved with Hungarian-algorithm or min-cost-flow style methods.

attention-head-shapes.name: Attention head shapes
attention-head-shapes.what: How you split a fixed attention budget between head count and head dimension — mathematically equivalent configurations can differ sharply in throughput depending on the accelerator's matrix-multiply dimensions.

ci-pipeline-tracing.name: CI pipeline tracing
ci-pipeline-tracing.what: Emitting CI workflows, jobs and steps as nested OpenTelemetry spans, so slow or flaky builds can be inspected like application traces.

comprehension-debt.name: Comprehension debt
comprehension-debt.what: The growing gap between how much code a system contains and how much of it any person actually understands, made worse when code is generated faster than it can be reviewed.

confidential-computing.name: Confidential computing
confidential-computing.what: Executing workloads inside hardware-attested encrypted VMs so even the infrastructure operator cannot read the data being processed — extending a device's trust boundary into the data centre.

contextual-integrity.name: Contextual integrity
contextual-integrity.what: A privacy framework that treats privacy as whether an information flow is appropriate for its context, now being applied to AI agents.

dbt.name: dbt
dbt.what: A tool that turns a folder of SQL SELECT statements into a tested, version-controlled pipeline that runs inside the warehouse in dependency order.

dns-tunnelling.name: DNS tunnelling
dns-tunnelling.what: Encoding data into DNS queries to move it past egress controls that only inspect HTTP — the canonical escape route from a network-isolated sandbox.

evaluation-benchmarks.name: Evaluation benchmarks
evaluation-benchmarks.what: Constructing a scored set of realistic cases with an explicit rubric, so a model or prompt change can be measured rather than guessed at — eval coverage is what sets your change velocity.

feature-stores.name: Feature stores
feature-stores.what: Infrastructure that computes, stores and serves ML features consistently between training and inference, so a model sees the same feature definition in both.

federated-learning.name: Federated learning
federated-learning.what: Training models on data that stays on user devices, with only privatised updates leaving the device.

gitops.name: GitOps
gitops.what: Deployment model where Git holds desired state and an in-cluster controller (e.g. Argo CD) continuously reconciles live state to it.

headless-browser-detection.name: Headless browser detection
headless-browser-detection.what: Telling automated (headless, CDP-driven) browsers from real users via API, rendering, network and HTTP/2 fingerprints.

hybrid-search-rrf.name: Hybrid search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion
hybrid-search-rrf.what: Combining vector and keyword (BM25) retrieval by merging ranked lists on position rather than raw scores.

load-shedding.name: Priority scheduling and load shedding
load-shedding.what: Under overload, deliberately drop low-priority work so critical work keeps meeting its deadlines.

matryoshka-embeddings.name: Matryoshka embeddings
matryoshka-embeddings.what: Embeddings trained so a prefix of the vector is still useful, which lets you truncate dimensions to trade quality for storage.

model-context-protocol.name: Model Context Protocol
model-context-protocol.what: An open protocol giving LLM agents a standard server interface for discovering and calling external tools and data sources.

model-flops-utilisation.name: Model FLOPs utilisation
model-flops-utilisation.what: The fraction of an accelerator's theoretical peak FLOPs a training run actually achieves — the headline efficiency number for large-scale training, and the thing hardware-aware architecture choices move.

multi-agent-orchestration.name: Multi-agent orchestration
multi-agent-orchestration.what: Coordinating several specialised models behind a controller that allocates work and scores results — often with a judge model supplying the reward and a persistent memory holding shared state.

nats.name: NATS
nats.what: A lightweight, very high-throughput pub/sub messaging system using subject-based addressing rather than queues and exchanges.

network-time-security.name: Network Time Security (NTS)
network-time-security.what: RFC 8915: a TLS key exchange plus authenticated NTP packets, so clients can verify where their time came from.

on-device-inference.name: On-device inference
on-device-inference.what: Running a model locally rather than calling a hosted API — enabling cloud-planner / local-executor splits where token-heavy work stays on the machine.

partial-indexes.name: Partial indexes
partial-indexes.what: A Postgres index carrying a WHERE clause so it covers only matching rows — smaller, cheaper to write, and often the fix for one slow filtered query.

penetration-testing.name: Penetration testing
penetration-testing.what: An authorised, scoped simulated attack: testers chain small weaknesses toward a goal and report the path and fixes.

prompt-caching.name: Prompt caching
prompt-caching.what: Reusing the computed attention state of a repeated prompt prefix across requests, cutting both latency and token cost; explicit breakpoints make the cache something you design rather than infer.

rl-post-training.name: RL post-training
rl-post-training.what: Training a model against a reward signal rather than labelled answers, to instil behaviour you can describe but not specify.

slsa.name: SLSA (supply-chain provenance)
slsa.what: Graded framework for proving how a software artifact was built: signed provenance, hosted and hermetic builds.

small-language-models.name: Small language models
small-language-models.what: Cheaper, faster model tiers traded off against frontier models for high-volume work and routing.

storage-compute-separation.name: Storage–compute separation
storage-compute-separation.what: Decoupling a database's query compute from its durable storage layer so each scales independently, enabling scale-to-zero compute and non-contending analytical reads.

streaming-feature-pipelines.name: Streaming feature pipelines
streaming-feature-pipelines.what: Moving feature computation from batch refresh to near-real-time push, so behaviour from seconds ago can influence the next prediction.

system-one-models.name: System One models (Jev)
system-one-models.what: Schema-constrained models that return typed decisions and calibrated probabilities rather than text — built for classification, routing and gating, where they cannot answer outside the schema you define.

tla-plus.name: TLA+
tla-plus.what: A formal specification language and model checker for concurrent and distributed systems — you state an invariant and it searches the state space for a sequence that violates it.

traffic-replay.name: Traffic capture and replay
traffic-replay.what: Recording real production queries and replaying them offline to load-test, capacity-plan and de-risk upgrades.

human-in-the-loop-approvals.name: Human-in-the-loop approvals
human-in-the-loop-approvals.what: Pausing an agent before a consequential tool call so a person can approve, reject or edit it.

step-up-authentication.name: Step-up authentication
step-up-authentication.what: Requiring a fresh, stronger proof of identity before a sensitive action, without ending the existing session.

media-over-quic.name: Media over QUIC
media-over-quic.what: An emerging IETF protocol that carries live and real-time media as tracks over QUIC, with relays that cache and fan out without parsing the media.

elastic-inference-capacity.name: Elastic inference capacity
elastic-inference-capacity.what: Running optional, preemptible work on idle accelerators and shedding it instantly when the capacity is reclaimed.

kv-cache-sharing.name: KV cache sharing
kv-cache-sharing.what: Reusing or transferring a model's attention key/value cache between requests, agents or even models, so shared context isn't recomputed.

monorepo-source-control.name: Agent-scale source control
monorepo-source-control.what: Version control built around an always-online server that answers history queries by API and serves sparse checkouts from caches, instead of every client holding a full git clone.

break-glass-access.name: Break-glass access
break-glass-access.what: A pre-arranged emergency path to elevated access that grants nothing until used, alerts people when used, expires on its own and is reviewed after.

recsys-foundation-models.name: Recommendation foundation models
recsys-foundation-models.what: One large central model trained on all of a platform's engagement data, whose knowledge is passed down to the small, fast models that do real-time ranking.

synthetic-training-data.name: Synthetic training data
synthetic-training-data.what: Training examples generated by a model, often grounded in real behaviour logs, used when there is no real labelled data yet.

postgres-lock-queue.name: Postgres lock queue
postgres-lock-queue.what: Lock requests on a table wait in arrival order, so a DDL statement stuck behind a long query also blocks every read and write that arrives after it.

mixture-of-experts.name: Mixture of experts
mixture-of-experts.what: A model architecture where a router sends each token to a few of many expert sub-networks, so compute per token tracks active parameters, not total parameters.

postgres-toast.name: Postgres TOAST
postgres-toast.what: How Postgres stores values too big for a row: it compresses them and, if still too large, moves them to a side table in chunks, which makes reading them several times slower.

mcp-skills-extension.name: Skills over MCP (SEP-2640)
mcp-skills-extension.what: An MCP extension that lets a server publish Agent Skills as resources with per-file digests, so hosts can load instructions lazily and tie approval to exact content.

skill-prompt-injection.name: Skill-file prompt injection
skill-prompt-injection.what: Hidden or malicious instructions inside skill and context files (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md) that an agent follows as if they were trusted guidance.

context-resets.name: Context resets (fork-and-flush)
context-resets.what: Clearing an agent's chat history while keeping its workspace, often across several parallel branches, to escape the ruts that summarised context keeps it in.

model-distillation.name: Model distillation attacks
model-distillation.what: Training a cheaper model on a stronger model's outputs, especially its reasoning traces, without permission, and the defences that limit it.

validation-bottleneck.name: Validation bottleneck
validation-bottleneck.what: When AI produces documents and code faster than people can check them, so review becomes the limit; answered by agentic reviewers that split and verify long documents.

outcome-level-delegation.name: Outcome-level delegation
outcome-level-delegation.what: Giving a model the goal behind a task (keep the app crash-free) plus the access and outside checks it needs, rather than one task at a time.

search-based-testing.name: Search-based testing
search-based-testing.what: Automated testing that treats finding bugs as a search problem, optimising several goals at once such as coverage, crashes found and short reproduction steps.

rbac.name: RBAC
rbac.what: Role-based access control: permissions are grouped into roles, users are given roles, and every check asks whether the user's roles include the needed permission.

react-compiler.name: React Compiler
react-compiler.what: A build-time compiler that rewrites React components so props, values and callbacks are memoised automatically, replacing hand-written memo, useMemo and useCallback.

tree-shaking.name: Tree shaking
tree-shaking.what: Dead-code elimination in a JavaScript bundler: exports nothing imports are dropped from the bundle, which only works when the bundler can prove the code has no side effects.

agent-least-privilege.name: Least privilege for agents
agent-least-privilege.what: Giving each AI agent only the tools, scopes and tokens its job needs, ideally short-lived, so a confused or hijacked agent can do limited damage.

agent-overreach.name: Agent overreach
agent-overreach.what: An agent going beyond what its task intended, often by working around a restriction instead of stopping when it cannot finish.

reward-hacking.name: Reward hacking
reward-hacking.what: When a model trained with reinforcement learning learns to get the reward through a loophole or workaround rather than the intended behaviour.

capacity-planning.name: Capacity planning
capacity-planning.what: Forecasting peak demand and provisioning headroom ahead of it, so spikes don't depend on autoscaling reacting in time.

slo-burn-rate-alerting.name: SLO burn-rate alerting
slo-burn-rate-alerting.what: Alerting on how fast an error budget is being consumed over several time windows, instead of on fixed metric thresholds.

internal-agent-platform.name: Internal agent platforms
internal-agent-platform.what: A company-wide coding agent that reaches internal systems and knowledge through standard tool servers, so teams share one way of giving agents context instead of building their own.

dpop.name: DPoP
dpop.what: Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (RFC 9449): an OAuth token is bound to a client's private key, so a stolen copy can't be replayed without that key.

independent-model-evaluation.name: Independent model evaluation
independent-model-evaluation.what: Outside organisations given deep access to an AI lab's models and practices so they can assess risk and publish their findings.

human-on-the-loop.name: Human-on-the-loop
human-on-the-loop.what: A way of working where the agent runs its own plan-build-test loop and the engineer sets the goal, watches and approves, rather than steering every step.

agent-evaluation.name: Agent evaluation
agent-evaluation.what: Testing an agent across multi-turn traces (tool calls, loops, cost and latency) as well as the final answer, usually with frozen scenarios and pass/fail judges.

multiplane-network-fabrics.name: Multiplane network fabrics
multiplane-network-fabrics.what: GPU cluster networks where each accelerator connects to several independent network planes and traffic is sprayed across all of them, for scale and fault tolerance.

next-concept-modeling.name: Next-concept modeling
next-concept-modeling.what: A non-autoregressive way to generate text: compress it into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy of discrete codes, then generate one level at a time with every code in a level predicted in parallel.

abac.name: ABAC
abac.what: Attribute-based access control: access is decided by comparing attributes of the user, the resource and the request (team, owner, environment) in a policy, instead of by named roles.

docker-on-macos-vm.name: Docker on macOS
docker-on-macos-vm.what: Containers need a Linux kernel, so on a Mac tools like Docker Desktop and Colima run a small Linux VM and point the docker CLI at the engine inside it.

package-manager-internals.name: Package manager internals
package-manager-internals.what: What a package manager actually does on install (resolve, fetch, extract, link) and the systems tricks, like fewer syscalls and copy-on-write file cloning, that make it fast.

tracer-bullet.name: Tracer bullets
tracer-bullet.what: A thin but real end-to-end slice through every layer of a system, built to prove the path works and then grown into the product rather than thrown away.

evaluator-in-the-loop.name: Evaluator-in-the-loop search
evaluator-in-the-loop.what: Letting a model iterate against an automatic checker that verifies correctness and scores each attempt, so it can search for better designs without a human between rounds.

thin-orchestrator.name: Thin orchestrator
thin-orchestrator.what: An agent architecture where the central router is deterministic and does no domain reasoning; it sequences work and enforces checks while isolated specialist agents do the thinking.

nothing-up-my-sleeve-numbers.name: Nothing-up-my-sleeve numbers
nothing-up-my-sleeve-numbers.what: Constants in a cryptographic standard whose origin is explained and reproducible, so nobody can suspect they were picked to hide a weakness.

training-goodput.name: Training goodput
training-goodput.what: The share of wall-clock time a large training job spends making real progress, after losses to failures, restarts and checkpoint rollbacks.

semantic-ids.name: Semantic IDs
semantic-ids.what: Representing each catalogue item as a short sequence of learned tokens, where similar items share tokens, instead of one opaque ID per item.

rebac.name: ReBAC (Zanzibar-style)
rebac.what: Relationship-based access control: permissions come from a graph of relationships (user owns folder, folder contains doc), and a check asks whether a path links the user to the resource.

connector-relays.name: Connector relays
connector-relays.what: An agent inside a private network opens an outbound tunnel to a relay, which forwards requests back down it, so a SaaS can reach internal services without any inbound firewall rule.

confused-deputy.name: Confused deputy
confused-deputy.what: A privileged component is tricked into using its own authority for a less-privileged caller, because it never checks whose request it is serving.

post-quantum-tls.name: Post-quantum TLS key exchange
post-quantum-tls.what: Hybrid TLS 1.3 key agreement (X25519 plus ML-KEM) that protects today's traffic against future quantum decryption, at the cost of larger handshakes.

progressive-disclosure.name: Progressive disclosure (agent skills)
progressive-disclosure.what: Structuring agent instructions so only a short description is always in context, and detail is loaded only when the agent decides it's relevant.

use-after-free.name: Use-after-free
use-after-free.what: A memory-safety bug where code keeps using a pointer after its memory is freed, so an attacker who refills that memory controls what the program reads.

software-supply-chain-attacks.name: Software supply-chain attacks
software-supply-chain-attacks.what: Compromising a trusted package or its release pipeline so malicious code reaches everyone who installs it.

speculative-decoding.name: Speculative decoding
speculative-decoding.what: A small drafter model proposes several tokens and the large model verifies them in one forward pass, giving the same output faster.
